catalog_quote: 3.1.3 Word-internal metrical structure. A distinction between metrically strong and weak positions in words is mainly relevant to syncope/apocope and stress/accent. In Tigemaxo, syncope and apocope are limited to short high vowels {u i} preceded by a sonorant, especially {r l n}. ... Tigemaxo tone patterns have few similarities to those of pitch-accent languages. Lexical tone melodies mostly begin with nonlow tone and include /H/, /M/, /HLH/, /HM/, and /HL/, the latter with subtypes. ... The lexical melodies are subject to grammatical tone overlays, for example dropping /H/ to all-low. Both H-Terracing, which produces level tone terraces extending beyond individual words, and the more local M-Terracing, are important in prosodic phrasing. Overall, there seems to be little or nothing to gain from analysing Tigemaxo words and phrases in terms of foot structure (iambic/trochaic etc.). Of c…

audit.reasoning: The 'tonal, no word-stress rule' coding rests on a 2025 open-access 674-page reference grammar by the language's principal modern describer, held held by the project with both deciding quotations verified verbatim at the stated pages (p.22 sec. 3.1.3; p.39 sec. 3.5). The author explicitly denies a weight-sensitive word-level accentual system and any role for foot structure, and describes a three-level H/M/L tone system with lexical melodies and grammatical overlays. The only older grammar in Glottolog (Blecke 1996) excludes phonology by the author's own statement as reported by Heath; the remaining Glottolog items are either mis-tagged syntax textbooks, a grammar of a sister language, or pre-tonology orthography/morphology works. sources.quote: Treats Tigemaxo purely as a three-level lexical/grammatical tone language with melody classes and phrasal H-terracing; no word stress or accent is mentioned anywhere in the article (a full-text search for stress/accent full text for stress/accent/metrical/foot: no Tigemaxo hits).
sources.locator: sec. 4 p.42-43 (ex. 2b: 'three lexical tone levels (H, M, and L): Cliffs, Tigemaxo'); sec. 8 'Tigemaxo' p.56 ('Tigemaxo has three lexical tone levels.. Bitonal melodies for nouns are /HL/, /HM/.. Multitonal melodies /HLH/, /HLHL/, /HLHM/.; H-terrace.. an H-toned string pronounced like a single word, with no phonetic marking of word boundaries'); p.42: Blecke 1996 has 'little information on tones or morphotonology'.
sources.note: Only dedicated phonology article touching Tigemaxo tone; downloaded now, confirms the three-level tonal analysis and is silent on stress. No other unheld work would improve this record: Blecke 1996 (Glottolog's top grammar) explicitly excludes phonology per Heath 2025 p.8.
